model.title: Which poem presents the cost of war more powerfully: The Charge of the Light Brigade or Poppies?

parts.text: Judge: Poppies, arguably, for a modern reader
Reason: one mother's loss is easier to feel than six hundred
Evidence: 'spasms of paper red' vs 'Rode the six hundred'
Qualify: Tennyson's scale is more stark

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: Arguably, Weir presents the cost of war more poignantly than Tennyson, because one mother's 'spasms of paper red' is easier to feel than 'the six hundred'; nevertheless, Tennyson's refrain conveys the scale of loss more starkly.

keywords.def: judge how effective something is, with reasons
a judgement with limits: 'more powerfully, although...'
words like 'perhaps' or 'suggests' that allow other readings

questions.q: Upgrade: 'Weir is good at showing sadness.'
questions.a: For example: 'Weir subtly evokes grief through ordinary objects such as the blazer and the poppy.'

questions.q: Add a qualifier to: 'Tennyson criticises the commanders.'
questions.a: For example: 'To some extent, Tennyson criticises the commanders, through the single line "Someone had blunder'd".'

questions.q: Core: in the portal response box, write an evaluative comparative paragraph: 'Which poem presents the effects of war more powerfully: Poppies or War Photographer?' Starter: 'Arguably, ...'
questions.a: A paragraph with a qualified judgement, evidence from both and evaluative vocabulary.

questions.q: Extend: underline every evaluative word you used
Stretch: write the counter-judgement in two sentences

options: Tennyson's refrain conveys loss more starkly than Weir's, although Weir's is more personal.
questions.a: A) Tennyson's refrain conveys loss more starkly than Weir's, although Weir's is more personal.. It judges effect and qualifies the judgement.

questions.q: Answer the ponder: how do you move from comparison to evaluation?
questions.a: For example: judge which is more effective for a purpose, with reasons and limits.
